candidate.summary: Adding a read-only JSON endpoint (/api/...) to spring-petclinic owners, vets, pets or visits
candidate.content: Put JSON APIs in a standalone @RestController (e.g. owner/OwnerRestController), not in OwnerController/PetController/VisitController: their @ModelAttribute methods run before every handler and throw IllegalArgumentException for unknown ids, which surfaces as 500 instead of 404. Look the entity up via the repository (OwnerRepository.findById) and throw ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND). Do not serialize entities directly (Pet.type becomes {id,name,new}); map to nested record DTOs (OwnerJson/PetJson with type as its name string, Lists via stream().map(...).toList()). Format with ./mvnw spring-javaformat:apply.

candidate.summary: Adding a read-only JSON endpoint (/api/...) to spring-petclinic; pattern used for owners and vets
candidate.content: JSON APIs live in standalone @RestController classes with record DTOs (owner/OwnerRestController, vet/VetRestController), not inside the HTML controllers: OwnerController/PetController/VisitController @ModelAttribute methods throw IllegalArgumentException (500) for unknown ids, so 404 must come from ResponseStatusException(NOT_FOUND) after a repository lookup. Map entities to records (names as strings, e.g. specialties via NamedEntity::getName; Vet#getSpecialties() is already name-sorted). The existing /vets resource wraps vets in {"vetList":[...]} with specialty objects, so a top-level array needs its own DTO list. Sort explicitly when order matters.

candidate.summary: Adding a CSV export endpoint (text/csv) to spring-petclinic
candidate.content: Reusable RFC 4180 writer: system/Csv (Csv.TEXT_CSV = "text/csv"; Csv.line(Object...) joins fields with ',' and ends with CRLF; Csv.field quotes a value containing , " CR or LF and doubles inner quotes; null -> empty). Endpoints go in their own @RestController (e.g. owner/OwnerCsvController) with @GetMapping(value="/owners.csv", produces=Csv.TEXT_CSV) returning a String built from Csv.line(header) + rows; a plain @Controller returning String would resolve a template. All owners: OwnerRepository.findAll(Sort.by("id")) (JpaRepository) since the custom finder is paged. Keep exports out of OwnerController: its @ModelAttribute throws IllegalArgumentException (500) for unknown {ownerId}.

candidate.summary: Adding a CSV export endpoint (text/csv) to spring-petclinic; Csv helper and per-entity CSV controllers
candidate.content: CSV pattern: system/Csv RFC 4180 helper (Csv.line(...) -> fields joined by ',', CRLF terminated; Csv.field quotes on , " CR LF and doubles quotes; Csv.TEXT_CSV) used from a standalone @RestController with @GetMapping(value="/x.csv", produces=Csv.TEXT_CSV) returning String (e.g. vet/VetCsvController). VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets") and returns an unordered Collection: sort explicitly (Comparator.comparing(Vet::getId)). Multi-value cells joined with ';' (specialties). Avoid putting /owners/{ownerId}/... handlers in OwnerController: its @ModelAttribute gives 500 (IllegalArgumentException) instead of 404 for unknown owners.

candidate.summary: Adding a token-authenticated JSON API route to microblog (app/api blueprint)
candidate.content: New API module app/api/<name>.py using `from app.api import bp` and `@token_auth.login_required` (app/api/auth.py; Flask-Login's login_required gives 302, not 401). Import the module in app/api/__init__.py (`from app.api import users, errors, tokens, posts`) or routes never register. db.get_or_404 inside the api blueprint yields JSON {"error": ...} via app/api/errors.py. SQLite returns naive datetimes: serialize as .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).isoformat() (+00:00), not isoformat() or +'Z'. Serializer helper post_to_dict(post): id, body, timestamp, language or None, author {id, username}. Post has no to_dict.

candidate.summary: Adding a paginated, token-authenticated JSON list endpoint to microblog's api blueprint
candidate.content: Pattern (app/api/posts.py get_user_posts): @bp.route + @token_auth.login_required; module imported in app/api/__init__.py. WriteOnlyMapped relations (user.posts, messages_received) need .select(); order newest first with id tie-break (Post.timestamp.desc(), Post.id.desc()); db.paginate(query, page=, per_page=, error_out=False); per_page = min(request.args per_page default 10, 100). Response: items (via a *_to_dict helper, timestamps .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).isoformat()), _meta {page, per_page, total_pages, total_items}, _links self/next/prev via url_for('api.<endpoint>', ...) with None when absent. Token user is token_auth.current_user(), not Flask-Login current_user.

candidate.summary: Adding a CSV export page for logged-in users to microblog (app/main routes)
candidate.content: Helper csv_response(rows, filename) in app/main/routes.py: csv.writer over io.StringIO (correct RFC 4180 quoting, unlike ','.join) and Response(..., mimetype='text/csv', headers Content-Disposition 'attachment; filename=...'); returning a str gives text/html. Routes use @bp.route + flask_login @login_required (anonymous -> 302 /auth/login; token_auth would give 401). WriteOnlyMapped relations need .select() + db.session.scalars. Timestamps: strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'), not isoformat. Order with explicit tie-break (timestamp asc, id asc). The existing /export_posts is an rq/Redis email job, not reusable.

candidate.summary: Adding a CSV export page for logged-in users to microblog (app/main routes)
candidate.content: Reusable csv_response(rows, filename) in app/main/routes.py (csv.writer into io.StringIO, Response mimetype='text/csv', Content-Disposition attachment). Routes: @bp.route('/...csv') + flask_login @login_required (302 for anonymous). Unknown user -> db.first_or_404(sa.select(User).where(User.username == username)). WriteOnlyMapped relations (followers, posts, messages_sent/received) need .select() and db.session.scalars; followers vs following are easy to swap; User.posts_count() for counts; write about_me or '' (not None). Times via strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'). Do not reuse views that write state (the /messages view sets last_message_read_time).

candidate.summary: Adding anonymous read-only stats/count endpoints in golang-gin-realworld (articles package, route wiring, author ids)
candidate.content: In hello.go, routes wired before v1.Use(users.AuthMiddleware(true)) are anonymous; anything after (or in ArticlesRegister/ProfileRegister) gives 401. Put handlers needing article data in package articles (articles imports users; reverse is a cycle) with an *AnonymousRegister func (ProfileStatsAnonymousRegister wired after users.ProfileRetrieveRegister) or in ArticlesAnonymousRegister/TagsAnonymousRegister. ArticleModel.AuthorID, CommentModel.AuthorID, FavoriteModel.FavoriteByID are ArticleUserModel ids (lazy row per user, user_model_id); FollowModel uses UserModel ids. Soft deletes: db.Model queries skip deleted_at, db.Table/raw joins (article_tags) do not. Nil []string -> null.

candidate.summary: Adding anonymous read-only stats endpoints in golang-gin-realworld (route group, soft deletes, user ids)
candidate.content: Anonymous GETs go in articles.ArticlesAnonymousRegister / TagsAnonymousRegister (wired in hello.go between v1.Use(AuthMiddleware(false)) and v1.Use(AuthMiddleware(true))); ArticlesRegister is authed (401). Handler pattern (articles/article_stats.go ArticleStats): FindOneArticle by slug -> 404 common.NewError; GORM model queries with Preload("Author.UserModel")/Preload("FavoriteBy.UserModel") since Author/FavoriteBy are ArticleUserModel rows, not UserModel. Model queries exclude soft-deleted rows; db.Table/raw SQL and article_tags joins do not (add deleted_at IS NULL). Start slices as []string{} (nil encodes null); sort with a tie-break.

candidate.summary: Adding a CSV export endpoint to golang-gin-realworld (articles package)
candidate.content: articles/csv.go writeCSV(c, [][]string): encoding/csv WriteAll into a buffer, c.Data(200, "text/csv; charset=utf-8", ...) (encoding/csv handles RFC 4180 quoting; not c.String/strings.Join). csvDateFormat = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999Z" with .UTC() matches the JSON API (RFC3339 does not). Query GORM directly (Preload("Author.UserModel"), Order("created_at ASC, id ASC")); FindManyArticle silently caps at 20. /api/articles.csv is registered with v1.GET right after v1.Use(users.AuthMiddleware(false)) (a Group("/articles") gives /articles/.csv). Author/FavoriteBy are ArticleUserModel rows: AuthorID and FavoriteByID are ArticleUserModel ids, not UserModel ids.

candidate.summary: Adding a CSV export endpoint to golang-gin-realworld (articles package)
candidate.content: Use articles/csv.go writeCSV(c, records) (encoding/csv, c.Data 200 "text/csv; charset=utf-8") and csvDateFormat "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999Z" (.UTC()). Per-article route: router.GET("/:slug/comments.csv", ArticleCommentsCSV) in ArticlesAnonymousRegister (anonymous; authed groups 401); other anonymous groups need their own *AnonymousRegister wired in hello.go before v1.Use(AuthMiddleware(true)). Unknown/deleted slug: FindOneArticle error -> 404. Usernames via Author.UserModel: CommentModel.AuthorID / FavoriteModel.FavoriteByID are ArticleUserModel ids; map a UserModel by user_model_id first. FindManyArticle pages at 20; sort with id tie-break.

candidate.summary: Filtering or changing a user's articles, comments or favorites in golang-gin-realworld (two user id spaces)
candidate.content: Articles, comments and favorites do not store UserModel ids: ArticleModel.AuthorID, CommentModel.AuthorID and FavoriteModel.FavoriteByID point to article_user_models (ArticleUserModel), a per-user row created lazily by articles.GetArticleUserModel(user) and keyed by user_model_id. The two id spaces diverge when users act in a different order than they registered. FollowModel uses UserModel ids. Map the UserModel first (GetArticleUserModel(u).ID, or lookup by user_model_id; a user may have none) then filter. Bug seen: ArticlesSerializer.Response passed myUserModel.ID to BatchGetFavoriteStatus (filters favorite_by_id), giving wrong favorited flags.
